cards.explanation: The answer is mercy. David says, "Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail…" (Psalm 6:2). He doesn't come in with a list of his good points. He just says he's frail and asks for mercy, and I think that's about the most honest way to walk into any prayer, friends.

The answer is False. David says, "Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are in agony." (Psalm 6:2). He calls himself frail and asks the LORD to heal him. Nobody flexing their muscles prays like that, and I love it.

The answer is True. David says his bones are in agony in verse 2, and then he says, "My soul is deeply distressed." (Psalm 6:3). So it's not only his bones that hurt, friends. Then he asks, "How long, O LORD, how long?" (Psalm 6:3).

The answer is the LORD's loving devotion. David says, "Turn, O LORD, and deliver my soul; save me because of Your loving devotion." (Psalm 6:4). He doesn't hand the LORD a list of his own good points. He points to the LORD's loving devotion, and I think that's a solid place to stand, bakers.

The answer is False. David says, "For there is no mention of You in death; who can praise You from Sheol?" (Psalm 6:5). Sheol is the realm of the dead. He says there's no mention of the LORD in death, and then he asks who can praise Him from there.

The answer is True. David says, "I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping and drench my couch with tears." (Psalm 6:6). All night, a flooded bed and a drenched couch. I think this one hurts, friends.

The answer is that his eyes fail from grief. David says, "My eyes fail from grief; they grow dim because of all my foes." (Psalm 6:7). After a night of weeping, his eyes are giving out. Grief and foes together will do that.

The answer is that the LORD has heard his weeping. David says, "Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard my weeping." (Psalm 6:8). That's the "for" in the verse, the reason he gives. A moment ago he was groaning, and now he's telling them to go.

The answer is accepted. David says, "The LORD has heard my cry for mercy; the LORD accepts my prayer." (Psalm 6:9). Verse 8 had the LORD hearing his weeping, and now it's his prayer being accepted. After all that groaning, that's a big turn, bakers.

The answer is that they will turn back in disgrace. David says, "All my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed; they will turn back in sudden disgrace." (Psalm 6:10). Notice the word sudden, friends. The psalm that started with groaning ends with enemies turning back.
